Elealeh
el-ee-AY-leh
proper noun
Hebrew Elaleh, “God is ascending” or “whither God goeth up”; a town near Heshbon, built by the Reubenites, later a city of Moab.

📖 Biblical Definition

Elealeh was a town in the good pasture-land east of Jordan, built (that is, rebuilt and fortified) by the tribe of Reuben near Heshbon: “And the children of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kirjathaim” (Num 32:37). The country was excellent for cattle, and the children of Reuben and Gad, having much livestock, sought and received their inheritance there. Its name, “God is ascending” or “whither God goeth up,” is a lofty one. Yet in later days Elealeh passed again into the hand of Moab, and the prophets took up a lamentation over it: Heshbon and Elealeh cried, their voice heard even unto Jahaz, when the joy of the harvest and the shouting for the vintage were made to cease. The town preaches the danger of the choice made by sight. Reuben and Gad chose their portion east of Jordan for its rich pasture, before the whole land was subdued, cleaving to the border and the world; and that eastern country was the first to be overrun and carried captive. Elealeh, whose name spoke of God ascending, became a Moabite town and a byword of wailing. The believer is warned not to choose his portion by the seeing of the eyes, like Lot toward Sodom or Reuben toward the eastern pastures, but to seek first the kingdom, lest the fair choice of the flesh end in loss and lamentation.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town near Heshbon built by Reuben, later a city of Moab and a byword of wailing (Num 32:37); a warning against choosing one’s portion by sight, like Reuben toward the eastern pastures.

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A town near Heshbon built by Reuben, later Moabite; it recovers the danger of choosing one’s portion by sight, cleaving to the border and the world.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A pasture-town raises no modern quarrel. Its history is a warning: Reuben chose the rich eastern land by sight, and that border-country was the first to be overrun and carried captive.

The principle to recover is not to choose one’s portion by the seeing of the eyes. Reuben and Gad chose the eastern pastures before the land was subdued, cleaving to the border and the world; and Elealeh, whose name spoke of God ascending, became a Moabite town and a byword of wailing. Like Lot toward Sodom, the choice made by sight ends in loss. Seek first the kingdom, lest the fair choice of the flesh end in lamentation.
